tool_args.rationale: The failed smooth saturating surface and large gradient-dependent shifts support the archive's two-layer siphon law: gradient-inhibited Michaelis saturation plus an open-sign square-root branch. Fit vmax, inhibition rho, and branch coefficient numerically to all paid rows; this is the most directly supported stationary mechanism and avoids further probes.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Gradient values already span 0.2 to 2.3, identifying inhibition; the archive gives a specific two-layer siphon form with a signed square-root branch term.
Existing ten rows include multiple inputs and gradients, and the selected static siphon law does not require horizon trajectories.
The prior fitted surface was refuted on fresh confirmation (RMSE 0.093839 > 0.045); the archive's explicit source-hub mechanism better explains the branch dependence.
All observations have the same H and mem_conv, so temporal/memory parameters are not identified; no evidence requires that higher-cost mechanism.
